Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""In-process build provenance records for registered resources.
2	
3	Each resource keeps at most one provenance record describing a single
4	build: the builder, a build number, a source summary digest and a list of
5	materials. Digests are normalized to lowercase and materials keep their
6	submission order. Nothing here is persisted: stopping or restarting the
7	service clears every record, no signatures are verified, and promotion
8	rules are unaffected.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import re
14	from dataclasses import dataclass
15	
16	#: A digest is exactly 64 hexadecimal characters; mixed case is accepted
17	#: but the digest is always stored and rendered in lowercase.
18	_DIGEST_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}")
19	
20	#: Text fields are non-empty and bounded by 256 Unicode code points.
21	MAX_TEXT_LENGTH = 256
22	
23	#: Fields accepted by the registration request; anything else is rejected.
24	_ALLOWED_FIELDS = frozenset(
25	    {"builder", "build_number", "source_digest", "materials"}
26	)
27	_REQUIRED_FIELDS = ("builder", "build_number", "source_digest", "materials")
28	_MATERIAL_FIELDS = frozenset({"name", "digest"})
29	
30	
31	class ProvenanceValidationError(ValueError):
32	    """A provenance payload failed field-level validation."""
33	
34	    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
35	        super().__init__(message)
36	        self.message = message
37	
38	
39	class ProvenanceError(ValueError):
40	    """A provenance operation could not proceed.
41	
42	    ``code`` is the stable, client-facing error code.
43	    """
44	
45	    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
46	        super().__init__(message)
47	        self.code = code
48	        self.message = message
49	
50	
51	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
52	class Material:
53	    """A single build material identified by name and digest."""
54	
55	    name: str
56	    digest: str
57	
58	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
59	        return {"name": self.name, "digest": self.digest}
60	
61	
62	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
63	class ProvenanceRecord:
64	    """The single build provenance record stored for a resource."""
65	
66	    builder: str
67	    build_number: str
68	    source_digest: str
69	    materials: tuple[Material, ...]
70	
71	    def to_dict(self, resource_id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
72	        return {
73	            "id": resource_id,
74	            "builder": self.builder,
75	            "build_number": self.build_number,
76	            "source_digest": self.source_digest,
77	            "materials": [material.to_dict() for material in self.materials],
78	        }
79	
80	
81	def _required_text(value: object, label: str) -> str:
82	    """Validate a required non-empty string of at most 256 code points."""
83	
84	    if not isinstance(value, str):
85	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(f"{label} must be a string.")
86	    if not value:
87	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(f"{label} must not be empty.")
88	    if len(value) > MAX_TEXT_LENGTH:
89	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(
90	            f"{label} must not exceed {MAX_TEXT_LENGTH} Unicode code points."
91	        )
92	    return value
93	
94	
95	def _require_digest(value: object, label: str) -> str:
96	    if not isinstance(value, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(value) is None:
97	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(
98	            f"{label} must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
99	        )
100	    return value.lower()
101	
102	
103	def build_provenance_fields(
104	    payload: object,
105	) -> tuple[str, str, str, tuple[Material, ...]]:
106	    """Validate a decoded provenance payload and return normalized values.
107	
108	    Returns ``(builder, build_number, source_digest, materials)``. The
109	    source and material digests are normalized to lowercase and materials
110	    are returned in their submitted order (an empty material list is
111	    allowed). Repeated materials (same name and normalized digest) are a
112	    validation error.
113	    """
114	
115	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
116	        raise ProvenanceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
117	
118	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
119	    if unknown_fields:
120	        raise ProvenanceValidationError(
121	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
122	        )
123	
124	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
125	        if field not in payload:
126	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
127	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
128	            )
129	
130	    builder = _required_text(payload["builder"], "Field 'builder'")
131	    build_number = _required_text(
132	        payload["build_number"], "Field 'build_number'"
133	    )
134	    source_digest = _require_digest(
135	        payload["source_digest"], "Field 'source_digest'"
136	    )
137	
138	    raw_materials = payload["materials"]
139	    if not isinstance(raw_materials, list):
140	        raise ProvenanceValidationError("Field 'materials' must be an array.")
141	
142	    materials: list[Material] = []
143	    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
144	    for position, raw_material in enumerate(raw_materials):
145	        if not isinstance(raw_material, dict):
146	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
147	                f"Material at index {position} must be a JSON object."
148	            )
149	        material_unknown = set(raw_material) - _MATERIAL_FIELDS
150	        if material_unknown:
151	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
152	                f"Unknown field: {sorted(material_unknown)[0]!r}."
153	            )
154	        for field in ("name", "digest"):
155	            if field not in raw_material:
156	                raise ProvenanceValidationError(
157	                    f"Material at index {position} is missing required "
158	                    f"field: {field!r}."
159	                )
160	        name = _required_text(
161	            raw_material["name"], "Material field 'name'"
162	        )
163	        digest = _require_digest(
164	            raw_material["digest"], "Material field 'digest'"
165	        )
166	        key = (name, digest)
167	        if key in seen:
168	            raise ProvenanceValidationError(
169	                "A material with the same name and digest is listed more "
170	                "than once."
171	            )
172	        seen.add(key)
173	        materials.append(Material(name=name, digest=digest))
174	
175	    return builder, build_number, source_digest, tuple(materials)
176	
177	
178	class ProvenanceStore:
179	    """Process-local storage of at most one provenance record per resource."""
180	
181	    def __init__(self) -> None:
182	        self._records: dict[str, ProvenanceRecord] = {}
183	
184	    def reset(self) -> None:
185	        self._records = {}
186	
187	    def remove_resource(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
188	        """Remove any provenance record for a resource.
189	
190	        An unknown id is a no-op.
191	        """
192	
193	        self._records.pop(resource_id, None)
194	
195	    def add(
196	        self, resource_id: str, payload: object
197	    ) -> tuple[ProvenanceRecord, bool]:
198	        """Validate and record the provenance for ``resource_id``.
199	
200	        Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``created`` is ``True`` for a
201	        first registration (HTTP 201) and ``False`` for an idempotent repeat
202	        of the exact same normalized content (HTTP 200).
203	
204	        Raises :class:`ProvenanceValidationError` for an invalid payload or
205	        :class:`ProvenanceError` with code ``provenance_conflict`` when a
206	        different record is already stored; the stored record is never
207	        overwritten.
208	        """
209	
210	        builder, build_number, source_digest, materials = (
211	            build_provenance_fields(payload)
212	        )
213	        record = ProvenanceRecord(
214	            builder=builder,
215	            build_number=build_number,
216	            source_digest=source_digest,
217	            materials=materials,
218	        )
219	
220	        existing = self._records.get(resource_id)
221	        if existing is not None:
222	            if existing == record:
223	                return existing, False
224	            raise ProvenanceError(
225	                "provenance_conflict",
226	                "A different provenance record is already registered for "
227	                "this resource.",
228	            )
229	
230	        self._records[resource_id] = record
231	        return record, True
232	
233	    def get(self, resource_id: str) -> ProvenanceRecord | None:
234	        return self._records.get(resource_id)

69	    """Validate a decoded JSON payload and return normalized field values."""
70	
71	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
72	        raise ResourceValidationError("Request body must be a JSON object.")
73	
74	    unknown_fields = set(payload) - _ALLOWED_FIELDS
75	    if unknown_fields:
76	        raise ResourceValidationError(
77	            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
78	        )
79	
80	    for field in _REQUIRED_FIELDS:
81	        if field not in payload:
82	            raise ResourceValidationError(
83	                f"Missing required field: {field!r}."
84	            )
85	
86	    name = _require_non_empty_string(payload["name"], "Name")
87	
88	    category_raw = payload["category"]
89	    if not isinstance(category_raw, str):
90	        raise ResourceValidationError("Category must be a string.")
91	    category = category_raw.lower()
92	    if category not in _CATEGORY_VALUES:
93	        allowed = ", ".join(CATEGORIES)
94	        raise ResourceValidationError(
95	            f"Category must be one of: {allowed} (case-insensitive)."
96	        )
97	
98	    digest_raw = payload["digest"]
99	    if not isinstance(digest_raw, str) or _DIGEST_PATTERN.fullmatch(
100	        digest_raw
101	    ) is None:
102	        raise ResourceValidationError(
103	            "Digest must be a 64-character hexadecimal string."
104	        )
105	    # Hexadecimal digests are case-insensitive; store them canonically.
106	    digest = digest_raw.lower()
107	
108	    source: str | None = None
109	    if "source" in payload:
110	        source = _require_non_empty_string(payload["source"], "Source")
111	
112	    return name, category, digest, source

115	class ResourceStore:
116	    """Process-local, insertion-ordered resource storage."""
117	
118	    def __init__(self) -> None:
119	        self._resources: list[Resource] = []
120	        self._by_id: dict[str, Resource] = {}
121	        self._key_to_id: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] = {}
122	        # resource id -> ids it directly depends on, and the reverse view.
123	        # Insertion-ordered dicts stand in for ordered sets: membership stays
124	        # O(1) while iteration remembers the order in which each relation was
125	        # established, which the global graph snapshot reports.
126	        self._dependencies: dict[str, dict[str, None]] = {}
127	        self._dependents: dict[str, dict[str, None]] = {}
128	
129	    def reset(self) -> None:
130	        self._resources.clear()
131	        self._resources = []
132	        self._by_id = {}
133	        self._key_to_id = {}
134	        self._dependencies = {}
135	        self._dependents = {}

137	    def list_all(self) -> list[Resource]:
138	        return list(self._resources)

140	    def query(
141	        self,
142	        *,
143	        category: str | None = None,
144	        name: str | None = None,
145	        digest: str | None = None,
146	    ) -> list[Resource]:
147	        """Return matching resources in creation order.
148	
149	        ``category`` is compared case-insensitively, ``name`` is an exact
150	        string match and ``digest`` is compared against the stored lowercase
151	        form. Multiple conditions are AND-ed together.
152	        """
153	
154	        if category is None and name is None and digest is None:
155	            return list(self._resources)
156	
157	        matches: list[Resource] = []
158	        for resource in self._resources:
159	            if category is not None and resource.category != category.lower():
160	                continue
161	            if name is not None and resource.name != name:
162	                continue
163	            if digest is not None and resource.digest != digest:
164	                continue
165	            matches.append(resource)
166	        return matches

168	    def get(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:

171	    def add(
172	        self, payload: object
173	    ) -> tuple[Resource | None, Resource | None]:
174	        """Validate and store a resource.

177	        the same category, name and digest are already registered.
178	        """

180	        name, category, digest, source = build_resource_fields(payload)
181	        key = (category, name, digest)
182	        existing_id = self._key_to_id.get(key)
183	        if existing_id is not None:
184	            return None, self._by_id[existing_id]
185	
186	        resource = Resource(
187	            id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
188	            name=name,
189	            category=category,
190	            digest=digest,
191	            source=source,
192	        )
193	        self._resources.append(resource)
194	        self._by_id[resource.id] = resource
195	        self._key_to_id[key] = resource.id
196	        self._dependencies[resource.id] = {}
197	        self._dependents[resource.id] = {}

200	    def add_remote(
201	        self,
202	        *,
203	        name: str,
204	        category: str,
205	        digest: str,
206	        source: str | None,
207	        resource_id: str | None = None,
208	    ) -> Resource:
209	        """Store a resource resolved from a remote repository.

211	        The caller has already validated the fields and matched the digest
212	        against the registry, so the record is constructed directly; the
213	        same uniqueness key is enforced defensively. When ``resource_id``
214	        is given it is reused (the caller already minted it during
215	        planning); otherwise a fresh id is generated.
216	        """
217	
218	        key = (category, name, digest)

220	        if existing_id is not None:
221	            return self._by_id[existing_id]

223	        resource = Resource(
224	            id=resource_id if resource_id is not None else uuid.uuid4().hex,
225	            name=name,
226	            category=category,
227	            digest=digest,
228	            source=source,
229	        )

237	    def discard(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
238	        """Remove a resource that has no edges yet.
239	
240	        Used to roll back a resource created during an aborted operation.
241	        Only safe for resources with no dependencies or dependents.
242	        """
243	
244	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
245	        if resource is None:
246	            return
247	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
248	        self._key_to_id.pop(
249	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
250	        )
251	        self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
252	        self._dependents.pop(resource_id, None)

254	    def remove(self, resource_id: str) -> Resource | None:
255	        """Remove a resource and every dependency edge touching it.
256	
257	        Returns the removed record, or ``None`` when the id is unknown.
258	        Edges the resource started and edges pointing at it disappear
259	        from both graph views; every other resource and edge is left
260	        untouched. The id is never reused by later registrations.
261	        """
262	
263	        resource = self._by_id.pop(resource_id, None)
264	        if resource is None:
265	            return None
266	        self._resources = [r for r in self._resources if r.id != resource_id]
267	        self._key_to_id.pop(
268	            (resource.category, resource.name, resource.digest), None
269	        )
270	        for dependency_id in self._dependencies.pop(resource_id, ()):
271	            dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
272	            if dependents is not None:
273	                dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
274	        for dependent_id in self._dependents.pop(resource_id, ()):
275	            dependencies = self._dependencies.get(dependent_id)
276	            if dependencies is not None:
277	                dependencies.pop(resource_id, None)
278	        return resource

280	    # --- Dependencies ------------------------------------------------------
281	
282	    def _reachable(
283	        self, start: str, graph: dict[str, dict[str, None]]
284	    ) -> set[str]:
285	        """Transitive closure of ``start`` through ``graph`` (start excluded)."""
286	
287	        seen: set[str] = set()
288	        stack = list(graph.get(start, ()))
289	        while stack:
290	            node = stack.pop()
291	            if node in seen:
292	                continue
293	            seen.add(node)
294	            stack.extend(graph.get(node, ()))
295	        return seen

297	    def _registration_order(self, ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
298	        return [r.id for r in self._resources if r.id in ids]

300	    def check_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
301	        """Validate an edge without mutating the graph.
302	
303	        Raises :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency``
304	        when the same-direction relation already exists, or
305	        ``dependency_cycle`` for a self loop or a relation that would
306	        introduce a cycle.
307	        """
308	
309	        if resource_id == dependency_id:
310	            raise DependencyError(
311	                "dependency_cycle", "A resource must not depend on itself."
312	            )
313	
314	        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
315	        if dependency_id in existing:
316	            raise DependencyError(
317	                "duplicate_dependency",
318	                "This dependency relation already exists.",
319	            )
320	
321	        # Adding resource_id -> dependency_id creates a cycle whenever
322	        # dependency_id can already reach resource_id.
323	        if resource_id in self._reachable(dependency_id, self._dependencies):
324	            raise DependencyError(
325	                "dependency_cycle",
326	                "This dependency would introduce a cycle.",
327	            )

329	    def add_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
330	        """Record that ``resource_id`` depends on ``dependency_id``.
331	
332	        Both resources must already be registered. Raises
333	        :class:`DependencyError` with code ``duplicate_dependency`` when the
334	        same-direction relation already exists, or ``dependency_cycle`` for a
335	        self loop or a relation that would introduce a cycle; in either case
336	        the graph is left unchanged.
337	        """
338	
339	        self.check_dependency(resource_id, dependency_id)
340	        self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
341	        self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None
342	
343	    def has_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
344	        """Return whether the direct edge ``resource_id -> dependency_id`` exists."""
345	
346	        return dependency_id in self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
347	
348	    def remove_dependency(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> bool:
349	        """Remove only the direct edge from ``resource_id`` to ``dependency_id``.
350	
351	        Returns ``True`` when the edge existed and was removed, ``False``
352	        when there was no such direct edge. Neither resource record nor any
353	        other edge is touched; transitive relations that survive through
354	        other paths are left to be recomputed by the read views.
355	        """
356	
357	        dependencies = self._dependencies.get(resource_id)
358	        if dependencies is None or dependency_id not in dependencies:
359	            return False
360	        del dependencies[dependency_id]
361	        dependents = self._dependents.get(dependency_id)
362	        if dependents is not None:
363	            dependents.pop(resource_id, None)
364	        return True

366	    def list_dependencies(self, resource_id: str) -> list[str]:
367	        """Return every reachable dependency id in registration order."""
368	
369	        return self._registration_order(
370	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependencies)
371	        )

373	    def shortest_path(self, start: str, end: str) -> list[str] | None:
374	        """Return the shortest directed path from ``start`` to ``end``.
375	
376	        The path follows dependency edges in their direction (the start
377	        resource depends on the end resource) and is reported as the list
378	        of node ids, ``start`` first and ``end`` last, with no repeated
379	        nodes. ``start == end`` yields the single-node path. Returns
380	        ``None`` when ``end`` is not reachable from ``start``. Among
381	        equally short paths the one whose nodes come earliest in
382	        registration order -- compared from the second node onward -- is
383	        picked, so the answer is stable.
384	        """
385	
386	        if start == end:
387	            return [start]
388	
389	        # Hops from every node to ``end`` along the edge direction,
390	        # computed as a breadth-first walk over the reverse graph.
391	        dist: dict[str, int] = {end: 0}
392	        queue = [end]
393	        for node in queue:
394	            for predecessor in self._dependents.get(node, ()):
395	                if predecessor not in dist:
396	                    dist[predecessor] = dist[node] + 1
397	                    queue.append(predecessor)
398	        if start not in dist:
399	            return None
400	
401	        order = {
402	            resource.id: index
403	            for index, resource in enumerate(self._resources)
404	        }
405	        path = [start]
406	        current = start
407	        while current != end:
408	            remaining = dist[current]
409	            # Every candidate continues on a shortest path; taking the
410	            # earliest-registered one at each step yields the stable pick.
411	            current = min(
412	                (
413	                    successor
414	                    for successor in self._dependencies.get(current, ())
415	                    if dist.get(successor) == remaining - 1
416	                ),
417	                key=lambda node: order[node],
418	            )
419	            path.append(current)
420	        return path
421	
422	    def all_shortest_paths(
423	        self, start: str, end: str
424	    ) -> list[list[str]] | None:
425	        """Return every shortest directed path from ``start`` to ``end``.
426	
427	        Each path follows dependency edges in their direction (the start
428	        resource depends on the end resource) and is reported as the list
429	        of node ids, ``start`` first and ``end`` last, with no repeated
430	        nodes. ``start == end`` yields the single single-node path.
431	        Returns ``None`` when ``end`` is not reachable from ``start``.
432	        The paths are ordered stably: by the second node's registration
433	        order first, then by each subsequent node's registration order.
434	        """
435	
436	        if start == end:
437	            return [[start]]
438	
439	        # Hops from every node to ``end`` along the edge direction,
440	        # computed as a breadth-first walk over the reverse graph.
441	        dist: dict[str, int] = {end: 0}
442	        queue = [end]
443	        for node in queue:
444	            for predecessor in self._dependents.get(node, ()):
445	                if predecessor not in dist:
446	                    dist[predecessor] = dist[node] + 1
447	                    queue.append(predecessor)
448	        if start not in dist:
449	            return None
450	
451	        # Enumerate every shortest path: from each node only the successors
452	        # exactly one hop closer to ``end`` can continue a shortest path.
453	        # The graph is a DAG, so the walk always terminates.
454	        paths: list[list[str]] = []
455	        stack: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = [(start, [start])]
456	        while stack:
457	            node, path = stack.pop()
458	            if node == end:
459	                paths.append(path)
460	                continue
461	            remaining = dist[node]
462	            for successor in self._dependencies.get(node, ()):
463	                if dist.get(successor) == remaining - 1:
464	                    stack.append((successor, [*path, successor]))
465	
466	        order = {
467	            resource.id: index
468	            for index, resource in enumerate(self._resources)
469	        }
470	        paths.sort(
471	            key=lambda path: tuple(order[node] for node in path[1:])
472	        )
473	        return paths

479	        order.
480	        """

482	        return self._registration_order(
483	            self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependents)
484	        )

507	    def list_edges(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
508	        """Return every direct edge as ``(resource_id, dependency_id)``.
509	
510	        Edges are grouped by the start resource's registration order; within
511	        one start resource they follow the order in which each relation was
512	        established. Manually registered and cross-reference-resolved edges
513	        are reported alike, since both flow through
514	        :meth:`add_dependency`.
515	        """

519	            for resource in self._resources
520	            for dependency_id in self._dependencies.get(resource.id, ())
521	        ]

523	    def graph_stats(self) -> dict[str, object]:
524	        """Compute whole-graph statistics from the current registry.
525	
526	        Counts nodes and direct edges, lists isolated resources, ranks
527	        resources by out/in degree and measures the longest dependency
528	        chain (in nodes). Manually registered and cross-reference-resolved
529	        edges are counted alike, since both flow through
530	        :meth:`add_dependency`. Everything is derived on the fly.
531	        """
532	
533	        ids = [resource.id for resource in self._resources]
534	        out_degree = {
535	            resource_id: len(self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ()))
536	            for resource_id in ids
537	        }
538	        in_degree = {
539	            resource_id: len(self._dependents.get(resource_id, ()))
540	            for resource_id in ids
541	        }
542	
543	        isolated = [
544	            resource_id
545	            for resource_id in ids
546	            if out_degree[resource_id] == 0 and in_degree[resource_id] == 0
547	        ]
548	
549	        # The graph is a DAG (cycles are rejected at registration time), so
550	        # the longest chain is the maximum successor-path depth. The
551	        # iterative postorder walk avoids any recursion limit on long
552	        # chains; ``depth`` counts nodes, so an isolated node scores one.
553	        depth: dict[str, int] = {}
554	        for root in ids:
555	            stack: list[tuple[str, bool]] = [(root, False)]
556	            while stack:
557	                node, expanded = stack.pop()
558	                if node in depth:
559	                    continue
560	                successors = self._dependencies.get(node, ())
561	                if not expanded:
562	                    stack.append((node, True))
563	                    for successor in successors:
564	                        if successor not in depth:
565	                            stack.append((successor, False))
566	                    continue
567	                depth[node] = (
568	                    1
569	                    if not successors
570	                    else 1 + max(depth[successor] for successor in successors)
571	                )
572	        max_depth = max((depth[resource_id] for resource_id in ids), default=0)
573	
574	        def ranking(counts: dict[str, int]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
575	            # ``sorted`` is stable, so equal degrees keep registration order.
576	            ordered = sorted(
577	                (
578	                    (resource_id, counts[resource_id])
579	                    for resource_id in ids
580	                    if counts[resource_id] > 0
581	                ),
582	                key=lambda item: -item[1],
583	            )
584	            return [
585	                {"resource_id": resource_id, "degree": degree}
586	                for resource_id, degree in ordered
587	            ]
588	
589	        return {
590	            "nodes": len(ids),
591	            "edges": sum(out_degree.values()),
592	            "isolated": isolated,
593	            "out_degree": ranking(out_degree),
594	            "in_degree": ranking(in_degree),
595	            "max_depth": max_depth,
596	        }
597	
598	    def dependency_closure_summary(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
599	        """Summarize dependency closure size per registered resource.
600	
601	        One entry per resource, in registration order, each with the fixed
602	        key order ``id``, ``direct_count``, ``closure_count`` and
603	        ``max_chain``. ``direct_count`` counts the resource's own outbound
604	        edges (manual and cross-reference-resolved edges alike);
605	        ``closure_count`` is the deduplicated reachable dependency count
606	        excluding the resource itself (zero for an empty closure);
607	        ``max_chain`` is the longest outgoing path counted in nodes and
608	        including the start resource, so a resource without dependencies
609	        scores one. Everything is derived on the fly.
610	        """
611	
612	        ids = [resource.id for resource in self._resources]
613	
614	        # The graph is a DAG (cycles are rejected at registration time), so
615	        # the longest chain is the maximum successor-path depth. The
616	        # iterative postorder walk avoids any recursion limit on long
617	        # chains; ``depth`` counts nodes, so a resource without
618	        # dependencies scores one.
619	        depth: dict[str, int] = {}
620	        for root in ids:
621	            stack: list[tuple[str, bool]] = [(root, False)]
622	            while stack:
623	                node, expanded = stack.pop()
624	                if node in depth:
625	                    continue
626	                successors = self._dependencies.get(node, ())
627	                if not expanded:
628	                    stack.append((node, True))
629	                    for successor in successors:
630	                        if successor not in depth:
631	                            stack.append((successor, False))
632	                    continue
633	                depth[node] = (
634	                    1
635	                    if not successors
636	                    else 1 + max(depth[successor] for successor in successors)
637	                )
638	
639	        return [
640	            {
641	                "id": resource_id,
642	                "direct_count": len(
643	                    self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
644	                ),
645	                "closure_count": len(
646	                    self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependencies)
647	                ),
648	                "max_chain": depth[resource_id],
649	            }
650	            for resource_id in ids
651	        ]

653	    # --- Dependency usage -----------------------------------------------------
654	
655	    def dependency_usage(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
656	        """Summarize, per depended-upon resource, who depends on it.
657	
658	        One entry per resource with at least one dependent, in resource
659	        registration order, each with the fixed key order ``id``,
660	        ``dependents``, ``dependent_count`` and ``max_dependent_chain``.
661	        ``dependents`` lists every resource that directly or transitively
662	        depends on the resource, deduplicated and ordered by resource
663	        registration order, and ``dependent_count`` is that list's length.
664	        ``max_dependent_chain`` is the longest path from any dependent to
665	        the resource, counted in nodes with both ends included; a resource
666	        that is only directly depended on scores two. Manually registered
667	        and cross-reference-resolved edges are counted alike; everything is
668	        derived on the fly.
669	        """
670	
671	        ids = [resource.id for resource in self._resources]
672	
673	        # The graph is a DAG (cycles are rejected at registration time), so
674	        # the longest path ending at each node is computed over the reverse
675	        # graph with an iterative postorder walk that avoids any recursion
676	        # limit on long chains. ``height`` counts nodes of the longest path
677	        # ending at the node, so a node without inbound edges scores one
678	        # and a node only directly depended on scores two.
679	        height: dict[str, int] = {}
680	        for root in ids:
681	            stack: list[tuple[str, bool]] = [(root, False)]
682	            while stack:
683	                node, expanded = stack.pop()
684	                if node in height:
685	                    continue
686	                predecessors = self._dependents.get(node, ())
687	                if not expanded:
688	                    stack.append((node, True))
689	                    for predecessor in predecessors:
690	                        if predecessor not in height:
691	                            stack.append((predecessor, False))
692	                    continue
693	                height[node] = (
694	                    1
695	                    if not predecessors
696	                    else 1
697	                    + max(height[predecessor] for predecessor in predecessors)
698	                )
699	
700	        usage: list[dict[str, object]] = []
701	        for resource_id in ids:
702	            # Resources nobody depends on get no entry, regardless of
703	            # whether they themselves depend on something else.
704	            if not self._dependents.get(resource_id):
705	                continue
706	            dependents = self._registration_order(
707	                self._reachable(resource_id, self._dependents)
708	            )
709	            usage.append(
710	                {
711	                    "id": resource_id,

146	## 依赖关系接口
147	
148	依赖关系同样只保存在当前进程内存中，服务停止或重启后随资源一起清空，不会写入任何文件，也不做任何签名或持久化校验。关系只在**已经登记**的资源之间建立。
149	
150	### 登记依赖：`POST /resources/{id}/dependencies`
151	
152	声明路径中的资源（起点 `resource_id`）依赖请求体中的 `dependency_id`。请求体必须是 JSON 对象，且只允许一个字段：
153	
154	| 字段 | 类型 | 是否必填 | 说明 |
155	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
156	| `dependency_id` | string | 是 | 被依赖资源的标识；非空，且不得包含 `/`、`\\` |
157	
158	成功返回 HTTP 201，响应体是描述该关系的紧凑 JSON，键序固定并以换行结束：
159	
160	```bash
161	curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/resources/$A/dependencies \
162	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
163	  -d '{"dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"}'
164	```
165	
166	```json
167	{"resource_id":"<资源 A 的 id>","dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"}
168	```
169	
170	冲突与错误：
171	
172	- 相同方向的关系已存在时返回 HTTP 409（错误码 `duplicate_dependency`），不覆盖已有关系或资源。
173	- 自环（起点与依赖相同）或会引入环的关系返回 HTTP 409（错误码 `dependency_cycle`），图的状态保持不变。间接依赖闭合为环同样会被拒绝。
174	- 已经间接可达、但尚不存在的直接边不算重复也不算环，仍以 HTTP 201 建立。
175	- 起点资源或 `dependency_id` 指向的资源不存在时返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `resource_not_found`），不会自动建资源。
176	
177	### 解除单条依赖：`DELETE /resources/{id}/dependencies/{dependency_id}`
178	
179	解除登记依赖路径同一路由之后的一条**直接边**：起点为路径首段的资源，被依赖资源由末段标识给出，只接受 `DELETE` 方法。请求不得携带任何查询参数，也不得声明非空请求体（显式 `Content-Length: 0` 视为空体）。
180	
181	成功返回 HTTP 200，按登记响应的固定键序回显这条关系，正文为紧凑 JSON 并以单个换行结束：
182	
183	```json
184	{"resource_id":"<资源 A 的 id>","dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"}
185	```
186	
187	- 删除只作用于图上这一条直接边：两个资源的登记内容与各条派生记录一律不动；跨仓库引用建立的边也按同样方式移除，引用记录与解析出的远端本地资源保持不变。
188	- 被删的边不再参与依赖查询、影响分析、晋级阻塞明细（含全局晋级阻塞汇总）与依赖漏洞传导等视图；这些视图都按剩余的边即时重算。因其他路径仍间接可达的关系照常出现。
189	- 删除之后再以相同方向登记关系会重新建立这条边，按既有口径返回 HTTP 201；跨仓库引用重提仍按既有重复登记拒绝（`duplicate_reference`），也不会自动把边重建回来。
190	- 起点资源不存在时返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `resource_not_found`），不改动任何既有状态。
191	- 没有这条直接边（含被依赖资源已注销、边随注销连带清理）时返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `dependency_not_found`）；重复删除同一关系返回同样的未找到结果，不影响其他关系、资源与游标。
192	- 路径中任一标识为空或含 `/`、`\\`，请求携带任意查询参数，或声明了非空请求体，均返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`）。
193	- `DELETE` 之外的方法返回 HTTP 405（错误码 `method_not_allowed`，`Allow: DELETE`）。
194	- 删除成功后资源列表与筛选分页的既有创建顺序不变，此前签发的列表游标继续可用。
195	
196	### 查询依赖：`GET /resources/{id}/dependencies`
197	
198	返回起点资源**可达的全部依赖**（直接与间接），形状为：
199	
200	```json
201	{"dependencies":["<id>", "..."]}

## 依赖关系接口

依赖关系同样只保存在当前进程内存中，服务停止或重启后随资源一起清空，不会写入任何文件，也不做任何签名或持久化校验。关系只在**已经登记**的资源之间建立。

### 登记依赖：`POST /resources/{id}/dependencies`

声明路径中的资源（起点 `resource_id`）依赖请求体中的 `dependency_id`。请求体必须是 JSON 对象，且只允许一个字段：

| 字段 | 类型 | 是否必填 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dependency_id` | string | 是 | 被依赖资源的标识；非空，且不得包含 `/`、`\\` |

成功返回 HTTP 201，响应体是描述该关系的紧凑 JSON，键序固定并以换行结束：

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/resources/$A/dependencies \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"}'
```

```json
{"resource_id":"<资源 A 的 id>","dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"}
```

冲突与错误：

- 相同方向的关系已存在时返回 HTTP 409（错误码 `duplicate_dependency`），不覆盖已有关系或资源。
- 自环（起点与依赖相同）或会引入环的关系返回 HTTP 409（错误码 `dependency_cycle`），图的状态保持不变。间接依赖闭合为环同样会被拒绝。
- 已经间接可达、但尚不存在的直接边不算重复也不算环，仍以 HTTP 201 建立。
- 起点资源或 `dependency_id` 指向的资源不存在时返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `resource_not_found`），不会自动建资源。

### 解除单条依赖：`DELETE /resources/{id}/dependencies/{dependency_id}`

解除登记依赖路径同一路由之后的一条**直接边**：起点为路径首段的资源，被依赖资源由末段标识给出，只接受 `DELETE` 方法。请求不得携带任何查询参数，也不得声明非空请求体（显式 `Content-Length: 0` 视为空体）。

成功返回 HTTP 200，按登记响应的固定键序回显这条关系，正文为紧凑 JSON 并以单个换行结束：

```json
{"resource_id":"<资源 A 的 id>","dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"}
```

- 删除只作用于图上这一条直接边：两个资源的登记内容与各条派生记录一律不动；跨仓库引用建立的边也按同样方式移除，引用记录与解析出的远端本地资源保持不变。
- 被删的边不再参与依赖查询、影响分析、晋级阻塞明细（含全局晋级阻塞汇总）与依赖漏洞传导等视图；这些视图都按剩余的边即时重算。因其他路径仍间接可达的关系照常出现。
- 删除之后再以相同方向登记关系会重新建立这条边，按既有口径返回 HTTP 201；跨仓库引用重提仍按既有重复登记拒绝（`duplicate_reference`），也不会自动把边重建回来。
- 起点资源不存在时返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `resource_not_found`），不改动任何既有状态。
- 没有这条直接边（含被依赖资源已注销、边随注销连带清理）时返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `dependency_not_found`）；重复删除同一关系返回同样的未找到结果，不影响其他关系、资源与游标。
- 路径中任一标识为空或含 `/`、`\\`，请求携带任意查询参数，或声明了非空请求体，均返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`）。
- `DELETE` 之外的方法返回 HTTP 405（错误码 `method_not_allowed`，`Allow: DELETE`）。
- 删除成功后资源列表与筛选分页的既有创建顺序不变，此前签发的列表游标继续可用。

### 查询依赖：`GET /resources/{id}/dependencies`

返回起点资源**可达的全部依赖**（直接与间接），形状为：

```json
{"dependencies":["<id>", "..."]}
```

```json
{"resources":["<id>", "..."]}
```

结果按登记顺序排列，**不包含起点自身**；没有受影响资源时返回空数组。

- 每条记录固定三个字段，顺序为 `resource_id`、`advisory_count`、`max_severity`。
- `advisory_count` 是该资源已登记的告警总数，不去重也不合并；`max_severity` 取告警中 `severity` 的最高值，四档从高到低固定为 `critical`、`high`、`medium`、`low`，比较忽略大小写；没有任何告警时 `max_severity` 为 `null`、`advisory_count` 为 `0`。
- 路径标识为空或含 `/`、`\\`，或请求携带任意查询参数，返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`），不读取业务数据；标识合法但资源不存在返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `resource_not_found`）；`GET` 之外的方法返回 HTTP 405（错误码 `method_not_allowed`，`Allow: GET`）。任何情况下都不改变状态。
- 本次不提供筛选与分页。

### 依赖接口的错误

- 路径标识为空，或含 `/`、`\\`，返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`），不执行任何操作。
- 请求体缺失、不是合法 UTF-8 JSON、顶层不是 JSON 对象、缺少 `dependency_id`、`dependency_id` 不是字符串/为空/含分隔符，或出现未知字段，均返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`）。
- 这些接口不接受查询参数；出现任意查询参数返回 HTTP 400（错误码 `invalid_request`）。
- 起点不存在时，两个查询接口都返回 HTTP 404（错误码 `resource_not_found`），且不改变状态。
- 对 `/resources/{id}/dependencies` 使用 `GET`、`POST` 之外的方法返回 HTTP 405（错误码 `method_not_allowed`，`Allow: GET, POST`）；对 `/resources/{id}/dependencies/{dependency_id}` 使用 `DELETE` 之外的方法返回 HTTP 405（`Allow: DELETE`）；对 `/resources/{id}/impact` 使用 `GET` 之外的方法返回 HTTP 405（`Allow: GET`）。
- 任何非法请求都不会新增或修改资源、关系或分页游标。

在按资源分别查询依赖漏洞传导之外，可以在服务根路径一次性取得覆盖**全部已登记资源**的依赖漏洞传导汇总。该入口挂在 HTTP 服务根路径上，路径为 `/dependency-vulnerability-impact`，只接受 `GET`，不提供筛选与分页；调用方不带任何参数，即可一次取回全部资源各自的依赖漏洞传导结果。该视图即时计算且只读，不落任何记录，也不改变按资源依赖漏洞传导视图的既有行为；其输入仍只存于当前进程内存，服务停止或重启后随资源一起清空，不写入任何文件。

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import io
import json
import unittest

from provenance_api.app import application, store

DIGEST_A = "a" * 64
DIGEST_B = "b" * 64


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    content_length: int | str | None = None,
    content_type: str | None = None,
    omit_content_length: bool = False,
    query_string: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
        length = "0"
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
        length = str(len(payload))
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body
        length = str(len(payload))

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    if not omit_content_length:
        environ["CONTENT_LENGTH"] = (
            length if content_length is None else str(content_length)
        )
    if content_type is not None:
        environ["CONTENT_TYPE"] = content_type
    if query_string is not None:

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import unittest

from provenance_api.app import application, reset_state
from provenance_api.cross_references import Resolution

DIGEST_A = "a" * 64
DIGEST_B = "b" * 64
DIGEST_C = "c" * 64
DIGEST_D = "d" * 64

UPSTREAM = "https://repo.example.invalid"
REMOTE_ID = "remote-42"
REMOTE_NAME = "remote-model"
DIGEST_REMOTE = "f" * 64
SOURCE = "https://repo.example.invalid/sources/remote-42"


def call(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    *,
    query_string: str | None = None,
    omit_content_length: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], bytes]:
    if body is None:
        payload = b""
    elif isinstance(body, dict):
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
    else:
        payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else body

    environ: dict[str, object] = {
        "REQUEST_METHOD": method,
        "PATH_INFO": path,
        "QUERY_STRING": query_string if query_string is not None else "",
        "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(payload),
    }
    if not omit_content_length:
        environ["CONTENT_LENGTH"] = str(len(payload))
    captured: dict[str, object] = {}

    def start_response(status: str, headers: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
        captured["status"] = status
        captured["headers"] = headers

    chunks = application(environ, start_response)
    return str(captured["status"]), list(captured["headers"]), b"".join(chunks)


def call_json(
    method: str,
    path: str,
    body: bytes | str | dict[str, object] | None = None,
    **kwargs: object,
) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
    status, headers, raw = call(method, path, body, **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return status, headers, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))


class DependencyDeleteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        reset_state()

    def _create(self, name: str, digest: str) -> str:
        _s, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            "/resources",
            {"name": name, "category": "code", "digest": digest},
        )
        return str(body["id"])

    def _add(self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str) -> None:
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies",
            {"dependency_id": dependency_id},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

    def _delete(
        self, resource_id: str, dependency_id: str
    ) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str]], dict[str, object]]:
        return call_json(
            "DELETE",
            f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies/{dependency_id}",
        )

    # --- Success and response shape ----------------------------------------

    def test_delete_returns_200_echoing_relation_in_registration_key_order(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)

        status, headers, body = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")
        self.assertEqual(
            list(body), ["resource_id", "dependency_id"]
        )
        self.assertEqual(body, {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": b})
        self.assertEqual(
            headers[0], ("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        )

    def test_delete_body_is_compact_json_ending_with_single_newline(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)

        _s, _h, raw = call(
            "DELETE", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies/{b}"
        )
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertFalse(raw.endswith(b"\n\n"))
        self.assertNotIn(b" ", raw[:-1])
        self.assertEqual(
            raw,
            b'{"resource_id":"' + a.encode() + b'","dependency_id":"'
            + b.encode() + b'"}\n',
        )

    # --- Graph semantics ----------------------------------------------------

    def test_only_the_direct_edge_is_removed(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(b, c)
        self._add(a, c)

        status, _h, _b = self._delete(a, c)
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        # a still reaches c through a -> b -> c.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [b, c])
        # The direct edge itself is gone from b's inbound view.
        _s, _h, impact_c = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{c}/impact")
        self.assertEqual(impact_c["resources"], [a, b])

    def test_removing_edge_on_one_path_leaves_other_direct_edges_intact(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(a, c)
        self._add(b, c)

        self._delete(a, c)

        _s, _h, deps_a = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps_a["dependencies"], [b, c])
        _s, _h, deps_b = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{b}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps_b["dependencies"], [c])

    def test_re_registering_same_direction_recreates_edge_as_201(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._delete(a, b)

        status, _h, body = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{a}/dependencies",
            {"dependency_id": b},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")
        self.assertEqual(body, {"resource_id": a, "dependency_id": b})

        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [b])

    def test_resource_records_are_not_touched(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._delete(a, b)

        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(r["id"] for r in listing["resources"]), sorted([a, b])
        )
        for resource_id in (a, b):
            status, _h, _r = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}")
            self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

    def test_deleted_edge_drops_from_release_blockers(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        self._add(a, b)
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{b}/lifecycle",
            {"state": "quarantined", "reason": "suspect"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "200 OK")

        _s, _h, blockers = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{a}/release-blockers"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            blockers["blockers"],
            [{"resource_id": b, "state": "quarantined"}],
        )

        self._delete(a, b)

        _s, _h, blockers = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{a}/release-blockers"
        )
        self.assertEqual(blockers["blockers"], [])
        self.assertNotIn("dependency_blocked", blockers["reasons"])

    def test_deleted_edge_drops_from_vulnerability_impact_closure(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(b, c)
        status, _h, _b = call_json(
            "POST",
            f"/resources/{c}/vulnerabilities",
            {
                "advisory": "CVE-1",
                "component": "lib",
                "severity": "high",
                "summary": "a bug",
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

        self._delete(b, c)

        _s, _h, impacts = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependency-vulnerability-impact"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry["resource_id"] for entry in impacts["impacts"]], [a, b]
        )
        # b itself still surfaces the edge's absence by reaching nothing.
        _s, _h, b_impacts = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{b}/dependency-vulnerability-impact"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [entry["resource_id"] for entry in b_impacts["impacts"]], [b]
        )

    # --- Not found ----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_missing_edge_returns_dependency_not_found(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)

        status, _h, body = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(status, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_not_found")

    def test_repeat_delete_returns_dependency_not_found(self) -> None:
        a = self._create("a", DIGEST_A)
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)
        c = self._create("c", DIGEST_C)
        self._add(a, b)
        self._add(a, c)

        first, _h, _b = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(first, "200 OK")
        second, _h, body = self._delete(a, b)
        self.assertEqual(second, "404 Not Found")
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "dependency_not_found")

        # Other relations and resources are unaffected by the repeated delete.
        _s, _h, deps = call_json("GET", f"/resources/{a}/dependencies")
        self.assertEqual(deps["dependencies"], [c])

    def test_missing_start_resource_returns_resource_not_found(self) -> None:
        b = self._create("b", DIGEST_B)

        status, _h, body = self._delete(phantom, b)

        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "resource_not_found")

        from unittest import mock

        resolution = Resolution(
            name=REMOTE_NAME,
            category="model",
            digest=DIGEST_REMOTE,
            source=SOURCE,
            raw=b"{}",
        )
        reference_body = {
            "repository": "partner",
            "upstream": UPSTREAM,
            "remote_id": REMOTE_ID,
            "digest": DIGEST_REMOTE,
        }
        with mock.patch(
            "provenance_api.app.resolve_remote", return_value=resolution
        ):
            status, _h, _b = call_json(
                "POST",
                f"/resources/{resource_id}/cross-references",
                reference_body,
            )
        self.assertEqual(status, "201 Created")

        _s, _h, listing = call_json("GET", "/resources")
        self.assertEqual(len(listing["resources"]), 2)
        remote_id = next(
            r["id"] for r in listing["resources"] if r["id"] != resource_id
        )

        _s, _h, deps = call_json(
            "GET", f"/resources/{resource_id}/dependencies"
        )

        self.assertEqual(

        _s, _h, refs = call_json(

        )

def build_batch_fields(
    payload: object,
) -> list[tuple[str, str, str, str, str | None]]:
    """Validate a decoded batch payload and return normalized field values.

    The top level must be a JSON object with exactly one field,
    ``vulnerabilities``: a non-empty array of at most
    :data:`MAX_BATCH_SIZE` elements, each validated exactly like a single
    registration payload. Returns one normalized field tuple per element,
    in array order.
    """

    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise VulnerabilityValidationError(
            "Request body must be a JSON object."
        )

    unknown_fields = set(payload) - {"vulnerabilities"}
    if unknown_fields:
        raise VulnerabilityValidationError(
            f"Unknown field: {sorted(unknown_fields)[0]!r}."
        )
    if "vulnerabilities" not in payload:
        raise VulnerabilityValidationError(
            "Missing required field: 'vulnerabilities'."
        )

    items = payload["vulnerabilities"]
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise VulnerabilityValidationError(
            "Field 'vulnerabilities' must be an array."
        )
    if not items:
        raise VulnerabilityValidationError(
            "Field 'vulnerabilities' must not be empty."
        )
    if len(items) > MAX_BATCH_SIZE:
        raise VulnerabilityValidationError(
            f"Field 'vulnerabilities' must not exceed {MAX_BATCH_SIZE} "
            "entries."
        )

    return [build_vulnerability_fields(item) for item in items]


def max_severity(severities: Iterable[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the highest severity among ``severities``, else ``None``.

    Comparison is case-insensitive and follows the fixed ordering
    critical > high > medium > low; the result is always lowercase.
    """

    best: str | None = None
    for severity in severities:
        normalized = severity.lower()
        if best is None or _SEVERITY_RANK[normalized] < _SEVERITY_RANK[best]:
            best = normalized
    return best


class VulnerabilityStore:
    """Process-local, submission-ordered vulnerability storage per resource."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # resource id -> alerts in submission order.
        self._records: dict[str, list[Vulnerability]] = {}
        # resource id -> (advisory, component) duplicates already seen.
        self._keys: dict[str, set[tuple[str, str]]] = {}
        # Every alert across every resource, in global submission order;
        # used by views that aggregate beyond a single resource.
        self._sequence: list[tuple[str, Vulnerability]] = []

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self._records = {}
        self._keys = {}
        self._sequence = []

    def remove_resource(self, resource_id: str) -> None:
        """Remove every alert recorded for a resource.

        Global aggregation views stop counting the resource's alerts

        self._dependencies[resource_id][dependency_id] = None
        self._dependents[dependency_id][resource_id] = None

    def _batch_reaches_start(
        self,
        start: str,
        node: str,
        tentative: set[str],
    ) -> bool:
        """Whether ``node`` reaches ``start`` with tentative batch edges.

        The graph examined is the current dependency graph plus, outbound
        from ``start`` only, the edges to the batch entries accepted so far
        in ``tentative``. Every batch edge shares the origin ``start``, so
        those tentative edges are the only deltas to consider.
        """

        seen: set[str] = set()
        stack = [node]
        while stack:
            current = stack.pop()
            if current in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(current)
            if current == start:
                return True
            successors = set(self._dependencies.get(current, ()))
            if current == start:
                successors |= tentative
            stack.extend(successors - seen)
        return False

        self, resource_id: str, dependency_ids: list[str]
    ) -> None:
        """Atomically record several edges out of ``resource_id``.

        Both the start and every depended-upon resource must already be
        registered (the caller checks existence); ``dependency_ids`` must
        come from :func:`build_dependency_batch_fields`, so it is a
        non-empty list of unique, non-empty, separator-free strings in
        submission order. Conflicts are judged per entry in submission
        order, and within one entry in the order self loop, in-batch
        repeat, existing same-direction edge, introduced cycle -- the first
        failure wins. Cycle detection accounts for the edges earlier in the
        same batch. The whole batch is atomic: a failure raises
        :class:`DependencyError` and the graph is left exactly as it was; on
        success every edge is established in submission order.
        """

        existing = self._dependencies.get(resource_id, ())
        accepted: list[str] = []
        accepted_set: set[str] = set()
        for dependency_id in dependency_ids:

        in ``tentative``. Every batch edge shares the origin ``start``, so

在单条登记路径之后追加 `batch` 一段，一次性为同一个起点登记多条被依赖边。只接受 `POST` 方法。请求体必须是 JSON 对象，且只允许一个字段：

| 字段 | 类型 | 是否必填 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dependencies` | string[] | 是 | 被依赖资源标识的非空数组，单批最多 100 条；每项非空，不得包含 `/`、`\\`，数组内不得重复 |

整批按原子方式提交：任何一项不合法或冲突都不建立任何一条边，图保持原样。成功返回 HTTP 201，正文按提交顺序逐条回显起点与被依赖资源标识，为紧凑 JSON 并以单个换行结束：

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/resources/$A/dependencies/batch \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"dependencies":["<资源 B 的 id>","<资源 C 的 id>"]}'
```

```json
{"dependencies":[{"resource_id":"<资源 A 的 id>","dependency_id":"<资源 B 的 id>"},{"resource_id":"<资源 A 的 id>","dependency_id":"<资源 C 的 id>"}]}
```
